correctness.rationale: The p-pebble invariant is a bijection of the selected underlying K_n endpoints. Before any move at most 2(p-1) root points remain, so every new two-subset can be mirrored at n>=2p, indefinitely. The p-round ordinary game uses the identical bound. For all 4<=s<=2p, the specified forest with r=min(p,s-1) edges and c=s-r path components occupies s root points; its edge-intersection graph forces exactly s vertices by the explicit path reconstruction induction. Its existential diagram has at most p variables and rank at most p. This proves both iff directions for every p>=2, as well as exact minimum rank/width, and the trivial p=1 boundary. Two independent finite scripts support small cases, without replacing the general proof.

value.rationale: This natural, canonical family L(K_n) has a complete p-variable spectrum for every p, with exactly 2p-2 classes and a sharp representative of size p(2p-1). The equality of minimum distinguishing rank and width at floor(m/2)+1 is a precise structural resource theorem, not merely a restatement of generic count-free pebble equivalence or a single small example. Path forests explain every exceptional root size. The assertion concerns all quantifier depths at fixed variable width, a substantive strengthening over a bounded-round support estimate.
